body.statement:
Fix \(b_0>1\).  Suppose that \(\mathcal B_J\) is the normalized local B-spline basis on a quasi-uniform partition and that its degree \(r\) satisfies \(r+1\ge s\) and \(2r+1>\sup_{a\in\mathcal A_{\rm H}}\alpha_a\).  Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\rm S}\), heavy arms, fixed folds, and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), the learner satisfies, up to a fixed power of \(\log n\),
\[
\sup_{d_a(x)\ge n^{-b_0}}
\left|\log\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\log\pi_a(x)\right|
=O_P(\delta_{a,n}),
\]
\[
\left|\int m_{a,\tau}(x)
\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)}\,dP_X(x)\right|
=O_P\!\left(J_n^{-s}+n^{-1/2}J_n^{(\alpha_a-1)/2}
+\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a}}n\right),
\]
and the corresponding relative-error square integral is
\[
O_P\!\left(J_n^{-2s}+\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a}}n\right).
\]
For \(J_n=\lfloor n^\xi\rfloor\) with
\[
\frac1{s(\alpha_a+1)}<\xi<\frac1{\alpha_a+1},
\]
there is a deterministic \(M_n\uparrow\infty\) such that
\[
E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1),
\qquad
\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|=o_P(1).
\]
At \(\alpha_a=s=3/2\) and \(J_n=\lfloor n^{3/10}\rfloor\), the log-error order is \(O_P(n^{-1/8}{\rm polylog}\,n)\), the signed-functional order is \(O_P(n^{-17/40}{\rm polylog}\,n)\), and the normalized interior discrepancy is \(O_P(n^{-1/40}{\rm polylog}\,n)\).
body.justification: This is the early kill test and now derives, rather than assumes, the corrected amplified oracle-transfer condition.
body.gap: Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder control a regular-overlap likelihood projection, not this singular signed Hall-boundary functional.
body.consumer: The lemma supplies a primitive flexible first stage for the non-Gaussian quantile argmin.

obligation.what_is_open: After applying the endpoint-safe learner correction, prove the uniform localized Fisher lower bound, score concentration, constrained random-Hessian inversion, and signed Riesz-functional expansion for the growing Bernoulli spline likelihood.
obligation.obstruction: As presently defined, the learner cannot fit a positive boundary exponent: \(d_a=0\) and \(\alpha>0\) imply \(p_a=0\), contrary to the global open probability-range constraint. The target is therefore false before the proposed definition correction. After that correction, the frozen core still contains no result controlling the fitted Hessian or the singular boundary coefficient, and assuming either control would assume the theorem's crux.
obligation.attempted: Checked feasibility of the exact constrained map, then tested the induced \(\alpha=0\) fit on the legal mixed witness. A fixed-degree polynomial norm argument on the first knot cell gives a diverging lower bound for the claimed truncated log approximation. I also retained the Hall normalization and rate-window arithmetic from the prior round.
obligation.partial_result:
The obstruction is already visible before any stochastic Hessian calculation.  Let \(x_a\) denote the unique chart endpoint, so \(d_a(x_a)=0\).  Under the present construction, every candidate with \(\alpha>0\) obeys
\[
p_a(x_a)=\exp\!\left\{\alpha\log 0+
\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}\beta_jB_{j,J_n}(x_a)\right\}=0.
\]
This violates the imposed condition \(p_a(x)\in(0,1)\).  Thus every feasible candidate has \(\alpha=0\), and the advertised singular boundary direction is absent.

This is not a harmless value-at-one-point issue for the asserted supremum.  On the mixed witness, \(d_1(x)=x\) and
\(\log\pi_1(x)=\alpha_1\log x-\log2\).  With \(\alpha=0\), the fitted log propensity is a polynomial of degree at most \(r\) on the first quasi-uniform knot cell \([0,c/J_n]\), for a fixed \(c>0\).  Put
\(\epsilon_n=J_n n^{-b_0}/c\), and rescale that polynomial to a degree-\(r\) polynomial \(q_n\) on \([\epsilon_n,1]\), after subtracting the constant \(\alpha_1\log(c/J_n)-\log2\).  If
\[
e_n=\sup_{\epsilon_n\le t\le1}|q_n(t)-\alpha_1\log t|,
\]
finite-dimensional norm equivalence for degree-\(r\) polynomials gives a constant \(C_r<\infty\) such that
\[
\sup_{0\le t\le1}|q_n(t)|
\le C_r\sup_{1/2\le t\le1}|q_n(t)|
\le C_r(e_n+\alpha_1\log2).
\]
Evaluation at \(t=\epsilon_n\) consequently yields
\[
e_n\ge \alpha_1|\log\epsilon_n|-|q_n(\epsilon_n)|
\ge \alpha_1|\log\epsilon_n|-C_r(e_n+\alpha_1\log2),
\]
and hence
\[
e_n\ge
\frac{\alpha_1|\log\epsilon_n|-C_r\alpha_1\log2}{1+C_r}.
\]
For \(J_n=n^\xi\) in the displayed subcritical window and \(b_0>1\), \(\epsilon_n\to0\), so this lower bound diverges.  It contradicts the claimed vanishing log-error rate.  The Hall calculation remains valid independently of this defect:
\[
t_{a,n}=(c_an)^{-1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},\qquad
h_{a,n}=(c_an)^{1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},\qquad
\frac n{h_{a,n}}\asymp n^{1/(\alpha_a+1)}.
\]
After the endpoint-safe learner correction is applied, the unresolved mathematical step is the localized random-Hessian expansion that produces the three asserted likelihood bounds.
